newsitem.title: UK: Remote Scottish island sticks to old Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Remote Scottish island sticks to old Christmas.

text.p: A remote Scottish island celebrated Christmas on Monday, refusing to recognise the calendar adopted by the rest of Britain nearly 250 years ago.
Foula, about 20 miles (30 km) west of the Shetland Isles' main island, is the only place in western Europe still relying on the calendar formulated by Roman emperor Julius Caesar.

Errors in the Julian calendar led to the introduction of a new calendar by Pope Gregory in the late 16th century. Acceptance of this Gregorian calendar spread throughout western Europe and it was eventually adopted by Britain in 1752.
But not by Foula and its population of 75. There, it's still December 25.
